funder_name: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (FCDO)
funding_summary: Covers an approved return airfare, full tuition fees (paid between the CSC and the university), a stipend of GBP 1,712 a month (GBP 2,000 for London-area universities), a study travel grant, a child allowance for some single-parent, widowed or divorced scholars (GBP 622 a month for the first child, GBP 154 for the second and third), and an individual needs assessment with extra support for scholars who disclose a disability.
summary: Full-time taught master's study at a UK university for candidates from 43 eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries (Bangladesh, Belize, Botswana, Dominica, Eswatini, Fiji, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Grenada, Guyana, India, Jamaica, Kenya, Kiribati, Lesotho, Malawi, Malaysia, Maldives, Mauritius, Montserrat, Mozambique, Namibia, Nauru, Nigeria, Pakistan, Papua New Guinea, Rwanda, Saint Helena, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Samoa, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Togo, Tonga, Tuvalu, Uganda, Vanuatu and Zambia). Applicants must be citizens of, or have refugee status in, an eligible country (or be British Protected Persons) and permanently resident there; hold at least a 2:1 first degree by September 2027, or a lower second plus a relevant postgraduate qualification; be unable to afford UK study without the award; be available to start by September 2027; and commit to returning home (a graduate or other visa to stay in the UK is not allowed). Previous UK master's study or a previous Commonwealth master's scholarship makes a candidate ineligible. Applicants use the CSC Central online system and must also apply to a nominator, usually a national nominating agency, since the CSC accepts no direct applications; nominators set their own deadlines and must nominate by December 2026.
source_publisher: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
route_name: CSC Central online system plus a nominating agency
deadline_source_text: The page says applications for 2027/28 closed at 16:00 BST on Tuesday 20 October and prints no year; 2026 is inferred because the cycle is 2027/28 and 20 October 2026 is a Tuesday. Nominator deadlines differ.

funder_name: Government of the Republic of Korea
funding_summary: The page lists airfare, Korean-language training fees, tuition and a monthly allowance but gives no allowance amount for degree programmes.
teaching_language: Korean or English (depends on the programme)
summary: Korean government scholarship with an undergraduate track (one year of Korean-language training, then an associate degree of 2 to 3 years or a bachelor's of 4 to 6 years) and a graduate track (master's of 2 years, doctoral of 3 years), with several sub-tracks such as General, Overseas Korean, R&D, Global Network, Research and International Organization. The applicant and both parents must hold non-Korean citizenship. Undergraduate applicants must be under 25 and meet a grade requirement (cumulative score of 80 percent, a top-20 percent class ranking or a required CGPA); graduate applicants must be under 40, hold a bachelor's or master's degree and have an average GPA of at least 80 percent. Separate terms apply to the Korea-Japan programmes and the Exchange Students Program.
route_name: Embassy track or university track (see the GKS notice board)
deadline_source_text: Typical pattern from the page, with no exact dates or year: undergraduate announcement and embassy-track applications in September and university-track applications September to November; graduate applications February to March. The application button showed that it was not an application period when checked.
